checkpoints: Building a fresh Vault client, calling approleLogin, and reading the secret inside the request handler adds two synchronous network round trips to every single request, which is exactly where the extra ~40ms per endpoint comes from.
Re-authenticating via AppRole on every request generates one login event per request in Vault's audit log, drowning the very signal that audit logging exists to surface.

With nothing cached, the request path depends on Vault being reachable on every call, so a transient network blip to Vault becomes a full outage for the service — availability is welded to the secret store's availability.

The login response carries a lease_duration field that this code discards; that value tells you how long the credential stays valid and should drive a scheduled background refresh instead of a per-request handshake.

Authentication and the secret read belong at bootstrap — a one-time step run before the app starts accepting traffic — with the resolved value held in memory (e.g., via a config service) and injected into consumers, so the request path itself performs zero Vault round trips.

Boot-time and runtime failures call for different handling: if Vault is unreachable at bootstrap, the service should fail fast and let its health check go red, since a service holding no real secret is unsafe to serve traffic; a runtime refresh failure, by contrast, should log a warning and keep serving the last known-good cached value rather than crash.

Scheduling the refresh at roughly one-third of the lease duration leaves two more retry attempts before the credential actually expires, giving headroom for a transient Vault issue to resolve before any request is affected.

Once the secret is cached with periodic refresh, a rotated credential reaches every running instance automatically within one refresh window with no redeploy required — but only if the rotation pipeline updates the secret store before triggering the refresh, since doing it in the reverse order leaves instances refreshing into a stale or half-written value.
